:::{#rem-countable-additivity-sum-exists}
#### The sum in countable additivity always has a value

By @lem-nonneg-series,
the right-hand side of the equation in @def-countable-additivity,
$\sumto{i}{\infty} \measure(A_i)$,
always has a value,
because each $\measure(A_i)$ is in $[0, \infty]$.
For example, if $\measure(A_i) = 1/2^i$ for each $i$,
the partial sums are $s_n = 1 - 1/2^n$, and the sum is $1$;
if $\measure(A_i) = 1$ for each $i$,
the partial sums are $s_n = n$, and the sum is $\infty$.

:::
